problem: The curve $C$ is the intersection of a surface $S,$ defined by $z=f(x,y),$ with the plane $y=1.$ Given that the point $P(-1,1,-1)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{x}=3{e}^{x+y}-\operatorname{ln}⁡|xy|$, which of the following gives a tangent vector to $C$ at $P?$

feedback.problem: The curve $C$ is the intersection of a surface $S,$ defined by $z=f(x,y),$ with the plane $x=-\frac{\pi }{2}.$ Given that the point $P(-\frac{\pi }{2},0,2)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{y}=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y}{2}$, which of the following gives a tangent vector to $C$ at $P?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface with the plane $x=-\frac{\pi }{2}.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve $C$ at the point $P$ will be given by the partial derivative ${f}_{y}(-\frac{\pi }{2},0).$ 

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ at $(-\frac{\pi }{2},0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(-\frac{\pi }{2},0) & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡0}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot 1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-f(-\frac{\pi }{2},0) & ={f}_{y}(-\frac{\pi }{2},0)(y-0) \\ z-2 & =-\frac{1}{2}y \\ z & =-\frac{1}{2}y+2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(-\frac{\pi }{2},0,2)$ can be given as the intersection of two planes:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-\frac{\pi }{2} \\ z=-\frac{1}{2}y+2\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that:

- For the plane $x=-\frac{\pi }{2},$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{1}=⟨1,0,0⟩.$

- For the plane $z=-\frac{1}{2}y+2$ (or $y+2z-4=0$), a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{2}=⟨0,1,2⟩.$

Finally, to find a direction vector for the tangent line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{n}_{1}\times {n}_{2} & =⟨1,0,0⟩\times ⟨0,1,2⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-2j+k \\  & =⟨0,-2,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a tangent vector to $C$ at $P$ is $⟨0,-2,1⟩.$
